questions.question: Q1 What is the purpose of a Power Distribution Unit (PDU) in a data center?

answers.b: To distribute electrical power to rack equipment

explanations.a: Incorrect. Cooling systems handle temperature management.
explanations.b: Correct. PDUs distribute power from the facility supply to individual servers and devices.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Data storage is handled by dedicated storage systems.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Network switches and routers provide connectivity.

questions.question: Q2 How many phases does a standard three-phase power system use?

explanations.a: Incorrect. A single-phase system uses one phase.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Two-phase systems are not standard in data centers.
explanations.c: Correct. Three-phase systems use three alternating current signals offset by 120°.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Standard systems use three phases.

questions.question: Q3 What is the angular separation between phases in a balanced three-phase system?

explanations.a: Incorrect. 90° is used in two-phase systems.
explanations.b: Correct. Each phase is separated by 120° in a three-phase system.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 60° is not the standard separation.

questions.question: Q4 What does the neutral conductor carry in a balanced three-phase system?

explanations.a: Incorrect. In a balanced system, phase currents cancel out.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The neutral carries the vector sum of phase currents.
explanations.c: Correct. In a perfectly balanced system, the vector sum of all phase currents is zero.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This only occurs under specific fault conditions.

questions.question: Q5 What happens when phase currents in a three-phase system are unequal?

explanations.a: Correct. Unequal phase currents result in a non-zero neutral return current.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Only individual phase breakers trip when exceeded.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Unbalanced loads do not necessarily reduce power consumption.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Voltage behavior depends on the specific imbalance.

questions.question: Q6 What is a circuit breaker designed to do?

answers.c: Disconnect the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit

explanations.a: Incorrect. Breakers limit current, not increase it.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Batteries and capacitors store energy.
explanations.c: Correct. Breakers protect circuits by disconnecting when current exceeds the rated limit.

questions.question: Q7 Which type of electrical load can cause harmonic distortion?

answers.c: Non-linear loads like switch-mode power supplies

explanations.a: Incorrect. Resistive loads are linear and do not generate harmonics.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Incandescent bulbs are purely resistive loads.
explanations.c: Correct. Non-linear loads draw current in pulses, creating harmonic frequencies.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Simple electric motors are approximately linear loads.

questions.question: Q8 Why is load balancing important in a three-phase PDU?

answers.b: To minimize neutral current and prevent overloading

explanations.a: Incorrect. Load balancing refers to electrical power, not network traffic.
explanations.b: Correct. Balanced loading minimizes neutral current, reduces losses, and prevents safety hazards.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Storage capacity is unrelated to power distribution.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Display resolution is unrelated to power balancing.

questions.question: Q9 What does AC stand for in electrical systems?

explanations.a: Incorrect. AC refers to the type of electrical current.
explanations.b: Correct. Alternating Current periodically reverses direction.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is not related to power systems.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Analog circuits are a different concept.

questions.question: Q10 What is a phasor diagram used for?

answers.b: To visualize the magnitude and phase relationship of AC quantities

explanations.b: Correct. Phasor diagrams represent AC signals as rotating vectors showing magnitude and phase.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Data storage uses different mechanisms.
